answers.explanation: There isn't. "Everything the vendor ships" is a good approximation, but vendors ship very different things.
The kernel loads at startup and stays in memory until shutdown.
System programs, like the shell and file utilities, come with the OS but run outside the kernel.
Applications are everything not associated with running the system itself.
That's why it's only an approximation.
System programs ship with the OS; application programs are everything else.
The kernel is the part that actually manages the hardware.
